## Strategy guide

**Thesis.** Nekro has a weak opening and must acquire technology indirectly, then turns opponents’ research into a flexible midgame toolkit. Repair the ship and infantry base, negotiate affordable combat access, and use stored money, cards, and technology to meet the objectives actually revealed. Keep a safe home system and more than one plausible final scoring route. Preparation is not scoring; confirm each objective’s prerequisites.

Source: SCPT 323, “Super Nekro Virus Guide,” published 2023-11-01. The guide says Nekro had no direct post-POK changes when recorded; compatibility with current rules is unreviewed. Claim IDs match the JSON. Times and segment IDs refer to the assigned ASR transcript.

### Opening and technology

#### C01 — Opening plastic

Treat the opening as a recovery phase: the starting Dreadnought gives fleet presence, but only two infantry and one Carrier leave limited capacity and weak early ground reach; prioritize plastic and expansion before chasing a technology engine.

Evidence: s000304,s000305,s000308,s000309,s000310,s001644,s001645; 1160.62–1199.84s; 6166.10–6177.72s.

#### C02 — Warfare priority

In round one, prefer another player taking Warfare; if no one will and the secondary is needed to repair the opening, take Warfare yourself, even when Trade is also attractive. Opponents can pressure Nekro by making it spend its own pick on Warfare.

Evidence: s000966,s000967,s000968,s000969,s000972,s000975,s000977,s001292,s001294,s001298,s001303; 3747.18–3797.36s; 4976.02–5016.68s.

#### C03 — Plastic before token spending

Do not spend the round-one economy primarily on Leadership tokens or Technology-secondary research when the opening still needs ships and infantry. Nekro cannot research; a Technology primary/secondary converts the research step into three command tokens, so buying plastic can address the more immediate bottleneck.

Evidence: s001163,s001164,s001167,s001168,s001169,s001170,s001171,s001172,s000426,s000431,s000432,s000433,s000434,s000435,s000436,s000437,s000438,s000439; 4538.86–4575.56s; 1657.36–1752.10s.

#### C04 — Trade when the opening allows

Trade is an excellent opening when it can fund plastic and payments that keep a target ship from retreating, but it is secondary to securing needed Warfare in the speakers’ recommended priority. Evaluate both cards against the opening bottleneck instead of treating Trade as automatic.

Evidence: s001285,s001287,s001288,s001289,s001292,s001297; 4957.46–5000.36s.

#### C05 — A negotiated, gradual technology plan

Track opponents’ technology acquisitions and plan small, controlled combats around them. The guide recommends a ‘tortoise’ approach: negotiate a modest target ship, pay its owner not to retreat, then destroy it to gain the technology while avoiding an unnecessarily costly early invasion.

Evidence: s001019,s001020,s001021,s001022,s001023,s001026,s001027,s001028,s001029,s001030,s001034; 3971.42–4038.40s.

#### C06 — Pay for the ship that stays

Make the no-retreat arrangement reciprocal: explain which ship Nekro wants to destroy, agree where the combat occurs, and compensate the opponent for losing the ship. The hosts reject the idea that opponents should donate technology access for free.

Evidence: s001600,s001601,s001602,s001604,s001605,s001606,s001607; 6000.08–6047.64s.

#### C07 — Exploit combat timing

Use the timing of Technological Singularity to gain technologies from units destroyed during combat, including Anti-Fighter Barrage and separate space and ground combats in the same activation. Look for multi-combat activations when several opponents’ units can be destroyed, rather than expecting non-combat destruction to qualify.

Evidence: s000386,s000387,s000397,s000398,s000405,s000406,s000407; 1463.74–1509.12s; 1510.10–1573.48s.

#### C08 — Anti-fighter barrage targets

Destroyer II is an attractive combat target because improved Anti-Fighter Barrage can destroy enemy units before later combat rounds and still trigger the technology ability; ordinary Destroyer II is useful even if Argent’s Strike Wing Alpha II is unavailable.

Evidence: s000413,s000414,s000415,s000416,s000418,s000420,s000421,s000422,s000423; 1590.86–1648.38s.

#### C09 — Gain versus research

Distinguish gaining a technology from researching one: the guide says Nekro’s copied technologies do not require prerequisites, while effects that would research instead yield three command tokens. It contrasts this with effects that explicitly gain a technology, which can still grant one.

Evidence: s000426,s000431,s000432,s000433,s000434,s000435,s000436,s000437,s000438,s000439,s000440,s000441,s000442; 1657.36–1752.10s.

#### C10 — Two Valefar slots

Treat Valefar Assimilator X and Y as two limited faction-text slots: on a qualifying technology gain, Nekro may put a token on an opponent’s faction technology and use its text. Replacing a copied unit-upgrade text can reveal the underlying upgrade again, so changing a token does not necessarily erase Nekro’s original upgrade.

Evidence: s000481,s000482,s000483,s000484,s000485,s000486,s000487,s000488,s000494,s000495,s000496,s000497,s000503,s000504,s000508,s000510; 1867.28–1936.78s; 1964.18–2000.20s.


### Fleet, leaders, and technology choices

#### C11 — Choose the Alastor’s job

The Alastor can serve as a hard home defense or as an offensive threat. Its start-of-space-combat ability lets Nekro’s ground forces participate as ships while staying on their planets; its printed capacity is less central to that use. Decide early which role the flagship should serve, then use other production for fleets sent outward.

Evidence: s000534,s000535,s000536,s000537,s000538,s000539,s000540,s000541,s000542,s000543,s000597,s000598,s000599,s000600,s000601,s000602,s000603,s000604,s000605,s000606,s000607,s000608,s000609,s000610,s000611,s000612,s000613,s000614,s000615,s000616,s000617,s000618,s000619; 2098.08–2165.94s; 2401.38–2521.40s.

#### C12 — Mechs with the flagship

Mordred’s combat bonus rewards fighting a player whose technology carries one of Nekro’s Valefar tokens. The Alastor’s ability to bring ground forces into space combat also makes carrying several Mordred mechs a substantial fleet option; the guide notes the token can be moved between combats to change which opponent triggers the bonus.

Evidence: s000620,s000621,s000622,s000625,s000626,s000628,s000631,s000632,s000633,s000637,s000640,s000641; 2521.90–2570.36s; 2571.30–2641.00s.

#### C13 — Leader economy and action cards

Use Nekro Malleon’s action-phase agent each round for two trade goods when the chosen player discards an action card or spends a command token, and value Nekro Acidos’s action-card draw after later technology gains. Together, these abilities support both cash and tactical card access.

Evidence: s000650,s000651,s000652,s000653,s000654,s000655,s000656,s000665,s000667,s000668,s000673,s000674,s000675,s000678,s000680,s000681,s000682,s000693,s000697; 2673.08–2753.68s; 2753.68–2853.76s.

#### C14 — A targeted hero gain

The hero offers a late tactical pivot: with Nekro units in a system, choose a planet with a technology specialty, destroy another player’s units there, gain trade goods based on that planet’s resource and influence values, and gain a matching-color technology. The guide recommends looking for a needed color or Integrated Economy through a yellow skip when the board supports it.

Evidence: s000738,s000739,s000743,s000746,s000747,s000748,s000749,s000750,s000751,s000752,s000753,s000754,s000757,s000760,s000761; 2954.50–3043.34s.

#### C15 — Integrated Economy remains contested

Integrated Economy is contested. One contributor argues an early round-three copy can multiply ground combats, technology gains, action cards, and control-objective reach; the hosts argue that saving the hero until a stage-two objective appears gives valuable information and can preserve cash that is not yet held. They favor waiting for the objective, while acknowledging an early Integrated Economy game can work.

Evidence: s000793,s000800,s000807,s000808,s000811,s000812,s000814,s000818,s000821,s000827,s000828,s000833,s000837,s000840,s000845,s000847,s000850,s000855,s000864,s000872,s000896,s000900,s000906,s000912,s000913,s000914,s000915; 3128.92–3305.96s; 3314.34–3585.86s.


### Strategy cards and objectives

#### C16 — Choose the prediction window

Use the prediction ability deliberately: it can be used once per agenda phase, so the hosts advise waiting past a low-value first agenda when a second agenda may offer a clearer For/Against prediction. They suggest seeking a roughly even split of votes when feasible and using Politics to influence which agendas appear.

Evidence: s000364,s000365,s000366,s000367,s000368,s000369,s000370,s000371,s000375,s000376,s000378,s000381,s000383,s000384; 1391.94–1463.32s.

#### C17 — Agenda and speaker control

Because Nekro cannot vote, the hosts recommend Politics as a way to control speaker and see the agenda cards, while using action cards and prediction to manage agenda outcomes. They caution against assuming round-one Custodians: the starting fleet is weak for the race and Gravity Drive is not guaranteed.

Evidence: s001042,s001046,s001047,s001048,s001049,s001050,s001051,s001052,s001056,s001058,s001059,s001243,s001244,s001245,s001246,s001248,s001250,s001253,s001257; 4068.34–4135.18s; 4798.52–4873.94s.

#### C18 — Leadership and Diplomacy

Nekro skips the Technology secondary, which can leave more strategy tokens for other secondaries; Leadership is therefore a lower-priority pick than for factions that need it to follow Technology. Diplomacy is situational, especially when readying a valuable planet helps meet a visible round-one objective.

Evidence: s001188,s001195,s001196,s001197,s001200,s001204,s001210,s001215,s001216,s001218,s001219,s001221,s001223,s001226,s001230; 4601.04–4685.68s; 4687.74–4783.44s.

#### C19 — Construction as an investment

Construction is usually a low-priority pick, but Nekro can spend its extra command-token flexibility on structure objectives and follow Construction when it is offered. The hosts frame Politics-secondary action cards and trade goods as a partial substitute for the Technology secondary, not an equally essential replacement.

Evidence: s001259,s001260,s001261,s001262,s001263,s001264,s001265,s001266,s001267,s001268,s001269,s001270,s001271,s001272,s001273,s001274,s001281; 4875.38–4956.64s.

#### C20 — Technology priorities

For technology priorities, the guide places Gravity Drive first among blue technologies, sees Bio-Stims and Neural Motivator as useful green options, and highlights Scanlink Drone Network and Predictive Intelligence as attractive yellow picks. Nekro’s command-token abundance can make Scanlink uses easier to afford, though Predictive Intelligence still offers late flexibility.

Evidence: s001341,s001342,s001344,s001347,s001348,s001349,s001354,s001359,s001360,s001361,s001365,s001366,s001367,s001376,s001377,s001380,s001381; 5141.98–5184.86s; 5184.86–5277.64s.

#### C21 — Unit upgrades and combat tech

Acquire useful unit upgrades whenever opponents make them available; the guide especially calls out Dreadnought II, Carrier II, and sometimes Fighter II for movement and board coverage. Duranium Armor and Assault Cannon are situationally attractive, particularly when a hero gain or combat timing can make them useful immediately.

Evidence: s001402,s001405,s001406,s001408,s001412,s001414,s001421,s001426,s001428,s001429,s001430,s001431,s001440,s001444,s001449; 5314.04–5444.20s; 5421.22–5486.50s.

#### C22 — Powerful faction texts

Treat faction unit-upgrade technologies as high-value Valefar targets because they add useful unit capabilities to a flexible fleet; the episode specifically praises Super Dreadnought II, Advanced Carrier II, Saturn Engine II, Strike Wing Alpha II, and Hybrid Crystal Fighter II. Other faction texts can be powerful but may create table-specific minigames or bargaining risks.

Evidence: s001454,s001455,s001457,s001458,s001459,s001460,s001468,s001471,s001473,s001475,s001477,s001479,s001485,s001489; 5490.20–5583.12s; 5583.64–5663.30s.

#### C23 — Situational utility texts

Look for utility faction texts that address a specific endgame need: the hosts cite Salvage Operations for late trade goods, Wormhole Generator for final-round access, and Aerie Hololattice for production. They also flag Nullification Field as a possible home-system wind-slay defense, while warning that value depends on the matchup and timing.

Evidence: s001502,s001503,s001504,s001505,s001507,s001510,s001511,s001512,s001513,s001514,s001518,s001519,s001520; 5708.40–5774.00s.


### Scoring and endgame

#### C24 — Diversify spare economy

Expect difficulty with Custodians and early points because the opening is slow and Nekro cannot dictate early technology access. Use the saved economy and command tokens to diversify into fragments, attachments, structures, and Politics when the board offers a credible scoring or denial opportunity.

Evidence: s001665,s001666,s001669,s001672,s001676,s001682,s001683,s001684,s001685,s001690,s001691; 6230.46–6299.94s; 6281.14–6313.86s.

#### C25 — Score opportunities safely

Take accessible bonus points and build toward objectives rather than sandbagging out of caution, but do not divert so much plastic that the main position collapses. Technology stage-one objectives are easier later than in rounds one or two; control objectives become attractive after Nekro repairs its ship and infantry base.

Evidence: s001702,s001703,s001704,s001705,s001706,s001707,s001708,s001709,s001710,s001711,s001712,s001716,s001722,s001724,s001727,s001728,s001729,s001733,s001734; 6331.44–6415.06s; 6418.44–6455.72s.

#### C26 — Late technology and spend objectives

Nekro can threaten stage-two technology and economic objectives late: the guide favors two and four technology colors when available and notes that the hero can fill a missing color; for spend objectives, reserve the hero’s unclaimed trade goods and action-card value as a surprise resource source.

Evidence: s001798,s001799,s001802,s001805,s001806,s001807,s001812,s001817,s001820,s001821,s001830,s001832,s001833; 6592.54–6639.58s; 6653.40–6713.38s.

#### C27 — Control and structure objectives

After acquiring movement and combat upgrades, Nekro can contest control objectives with a broad mix such as Carrier II, Light/Wave Deflector, Cruiser II, mechs, and Dreadnought II. The guide sees this breadth as a late-game strength and recommends pursuing structure objectives when the investment is affordable.

Evidence: s001836,s001838,s001843,s001845,s001846,s001847,s001850,s001852,s001855,s001858,s001859,s001860,s001861; 6714.00–6798.52s; 6798.52–6817.56s.

#### C28 — Secret objectives

Keep action-phase secret objectives that match Nekro’s evolving technology access; the guide recommends pivoting at the end when a newly copied technology completes a requirement. A faction-technology secret is treated differently: the hosts say Nekro must actually have Valefar copying faction text to satisfy it.

Evidence: s001872,s001877,s001878,s001879,s001880,s001881,s001882,s001884,s001885,s001886; 6847.68–6901.44s; 6903.02–6921.40s.

#### C29 — A tempo-based flagship line

If Nekro has established a lead in tempo by rounds two or three, protect speaker control and consider a forward space dock with Sling Relay: the guide proposes using the Alastor offensively early, then returning it to home defense later. This combines flexible production with a hard-to-attack home system.

Evidence: s001890,s001891,s001892,s001893,s001894,s001895,s001896,s001897,s001898,s001900,s001901,s001902; 6927.14–6992.86s.

#### C30 — Finish with multiple routes

The guide’s preferred finish is to stay on public-objective tempo, collect a bonus point when safely available, retain speaker for the late game, and protect home from a wind-slay. In the final round, a well-positioned Nekro may have multiple scoring routes, including a stage-two objective or relinquishing Support for the Throne if the remaining points still win.

Evidence: s001912,s001913,s001914,s001915,s001916,s001917,s001918,s001919,s001920,s001921,s001922,s001923,s001924; 7032.26–7112.14s.

### Component connections

Conditional interactions described in the guide; the links are not independent confirmation of current rules.
- `ability:technological_singularity` enables `technology:vax`: A qualifying combat technology gain can instead place Valefar X on the opponent’s faction technology under the episode’s reading. Evidence: 1867.28–1886.30s.
- `ability:technological_singularity` enables `technology:vay`: A qualifying combat technology gain can instead place Valefar Y on the opponent’s faction technology under the episode’s reading. Evidence: 1867.28–1886.30s.
- `unit:nekro_flagship` synergizes-with `unit:nekro_mech`: The Alastor can bring ground forces into a space combat and Mordred’s combat value then contributes to that combat; the connection is most relevant to an offensive flagship plan. Evidence: 2098.08–2165.94s; 2571.30–2641.00s.
- `leader:nekrohero` enables `technology:ie`: When a yellow specialty is available and the objective/map justify it, the hero can gain a matching-color technology; the speakers discuss Integrated Economy as one conditional target. Evidence: 2954.50–3043.34s; 3314.34–3565.10s.
- `leader:nekroagent` synergizes-with `leader:nekrocommander`: The agent can create two trade goods when another player accepts its cost; the commander can draw an action card after a later qualifying technology gain, and its draw can support another agent payment only if the card is expendable. Evidence: 2673.08–2753.68s; 2753.68–2792.28s.
- `technology:sr` enables `unit:nekro_flagship`: Sling Relay is proposed as a route to a forward dock from which the flagship can act offensively before returning to defend home; this requires the card, timing, and board position. Evidence: 6970.78–6992.86s.
- `strategy-card:pok6warfare` conflicts-with `strategy-card:pok5trade`: In the guide’s round-one priority, taking needed Warfare can mean forgoing the otherwise attractive Trade pick. Evidence: 4976.02–5000.36s.
- `technology:dd2` enables `ability:technological_singularity`: Destroyer II’s Anti-Fighter Barrage can destroy an opponent’s unit during combat, creating a stated opportunity for the combat technology gain. Evidence: 1590.86–1648.38s.
- `strategy-card:pok8imperial` scores `faction:nekro`: The guide recommends an Imperial pick when it can secure a bonus point such as Mecatol Rex, unless doing so diverts too much plastic or creates unacceptable risk. Evidence: 6331.44–6367.08s.

### Disagreement and source limits

Integrated Economy timing is disputed: one contributor reports a successful early round-three plan, while the hosts favor waiting for the stage-two objective and its information; they still allow early use when repeated ground combats repay it. The offensive Alastor plan depends on movement access, production, and tempo. The hosts call several faction technologies powerful or amusing as strategic opinion, not rules status. Transcript text is ASR with overlapping segments; no speaker attribution is claimed. Proper nouns are normalized only where the component reference supports them. Citations establish what this guide says, not current rules legality.

## Combined source guidance

The guide above contains conditional, transcript-cited advice. The pinned documents below add community research and a bot-oriented mid/late-game profile. Their ordered technology/build lists are proposals, not unconditional policy targets. Keep source disagreements and expansion assumptions visible.

**Historical scope:** upstream statements about available factions, engine support, bot behavior and benchmark results describe that source revision; they are not checks of this checkout. Podcast timestamps in upstream notes are approximate and do not share the local transcript verification.

<details><summary>upstream-community — The Nekro Virus (`nekro`)</summary>

[Exact pinned section](../sources/upstream-community.md#the-nekro-virus-nekro) · [Repository source](https://github.com/Feelx234/TI4-Bot-Dev/blob/1fd3092ad83a72bc3e379ac3946852b409adee6d/crates/ti4-server/docs/COMMUNITY_FACTION_STRATEGIES.md#the-nekro-virus-nekro)

> Historical source excerpt; advice and engine claims retain the source’s assumptions.

**Engine check.** Home Mordai II 4/0; start 1 dreadnought, 1 carrier, 1 cruiser, 2 fighters, 2
infantry, dock; starting tech Daxcive Animators. Propagation: cannot research; a research gives 3
command tokens instead. Technological Singularity: once per combat, after an opponent's unit dies,
gain one of their technologies. Galactic Threat: cannot vote; predict an agenda outcome to copy a
technology from a player who voted that way. Valefar Assimilators X/Y copy faction technologies.
Flagship: ground forces fight in space. Commander (3 technologies): an action card per technology
gained.

**Opening and cards.** The best-known guide says: be the tortoise, not the hare. Grow in rounds 1-2
(units, planets, both resource and influence), do not throw ships at fights just for technology,
start "space risk" from round 3. Card order round 1: Trade (others spend on research while Nekro
builds, and trading calms neighbours), then Leadership (deny the table tokens), then Technology or
Politics, then Construction (PDS at home), Warfare last; never Diplomacy or Imperial in round 1.
Politics in round 2 for the speaker token, which breaks agenda ties so predictions land
([BGG "Nekro - Be the tortoise, not the hare", 2019](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2283392)).

**Technology.** Copy movement first (Gravity Drive, unit upgrades): each copied movement tech
opens fights for more technology. Dreadnought II and Cruiser II are the staples; Destroyer II makes
farming technology from anyone easy; no more than two technologies of one colour; prefer unit
upgrades, then two technologies in each of four colours. Pay neighbours to "feed" you a fighter for
a technology rather than fight them (same guide).

**Builds.** Mass: big clumps of units win fights with small losses; bombard every planet; produce
2-4 infantry at home every round; the flagship is best as a home defender with many infantry.

**Diplomacy.** Players fear Nekro; play nice early, buy peace, be fair; Nekro is eliminated more
often than anyone but Winnu when played thematically aggressive. Table counters: deny tech tempo
(do not research deep near Nekro), and the Antivirus note
([BGG 2019](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2336546)).

**Matchups.** Counters Jol-Nar (tech-rich, -1 combat); takes Sol's Spec Ops II; PDS II networks
are the hardest problem (bring a bigger fleet, strike the centre).

**Strength.** SCPT top row in 2022 (PoK), A in async PoK data, B in SCPT 2025 (game too fast in
Thunder's Edge for a round-5 faction).

**Bot feasibility.**
- Research prompts become "gain 3 command tokens" (engine) and Technological Singularity picks a
  technology from the opponent: choose by a fixed preference (movement > unit upgrades the bot
  builds > colours it lacks). Value high for Nekro, effort S-M (needs the prompt id from
  `nekro.rs`).
- Targeting: favour fights against seats with valuable technologies the bot lacks; a destroyed
  fighter is enough. `activation_value` could add a bonus per "new technology the defender owns".
  Value high, effort M.
- Draft: Trade/Leadership up, Warfare down in round 1 for Nekro. Effort S.
- Galactic Threat prediction: predict the outcome most votes are already on (the bot cannot see
  intentions before voting; use speaker/current tally if exposed). Value medium, effort M-L
  (agenda handling is random today).
- Hard: buying peace and arranging "feed me a fighter" deals.

</details>

## Strategy connections

- [Technological Singularity](../components.md#ability-technological-singularity) **enables** [Valefar Assimilator X](../components.md#technology-vax). A qualifying combat technology gain can instead place Valefar X on the opponent’s faction technology under the episode’s reading. Sources: [SCPT 323, 1867.28–1886.30s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/323-super-nekro-virus-guide/)
- [Technological Singularity](../components.md#ability-technological-singularity) **enables** [Valefar Assimilator Y](../components.md#technology-vay). A qualifying combat technology gain can instead place Valefar Y on the opponent’s faction technology under the episode’s reading. Sources: [SCPT 323, 1867.28–1886.30s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/323-super-nekro-virus-guide/)
- [The Alastor](../components.md#unit-nekro-flagship) **synergizes-with** [Mordred](../components.md#unit-nekro-mech). The Alastor can bring ground forces into a space combat and Mordred’s combat value then contributes to that combat; the connection is most relevant to an offensive flagship plan. Sources: [SCPT 323, 2098.08–2165.94s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/323-super-nekro-virus-guide/); [SCPT 323, 2571.30–2641.00s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/323-super-nekro-virus-guide/)
- [UNIT.DSGN.FLAYESH](../components.md#leader-nekrohero) **enables** [Integrated Economy](../components.md#technology-ie). When a yellow specialty is available and the objective/map justify it, the hero can gain a matching-color technology; the speakers discuss Integrated Economy as one conditional target. Sources: [SCPT 323, 2954.50–3043.34s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/323-super-nekro-virus-guide/); [SCPT 323, 3314.34–3565.10s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/323-super-nekro-virus-guide/)
- [Nekro Malleon](../components.md#leader-nekroagent) **synergizes-with** [Nekro Acidos](../components.md#leader-nekrocommander). The agent can create two trade goods when another player accepts its cost; the commander can draw an action card after a later qualifying technology gain, and its draw can support another agent payment only if the card is expendable. Sources: [SCPT 323, 2673.08–2753.68s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/323-super-nekro-virus-guide/); [SCPT 323, 2753.68–2792.28s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/323-super-nekro-virus-guide/)
- [Sling Relay](../components.md#technology-sr) **enables** [The Alastor](../components.md#unit-nekro-flagship). Sling Relay is proposed as a route to a forward dock from which the flagship can act offensively before returning to defend home; this requires the card, timing, and board position. Sources: [SCPT 323, 6970.78–6992.86s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/323-super-nekro-virus-guide/)
- [Warfare](../components.md#strategy-card-pok6warfare) **conflicts-with** [Trade](../components.md#strategy-card-pok5trade). In the guide’s round-one priority, taking needed Warfare can mean forgoing the otherwise attractive Trade pick. Sources: [SCPT 323, 4976.02–5000.36s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/323-super-nekro-virus-guide/)
- [Destroyer II](../components.md#technology-dd2) **enables** [Technological Singularity](../components.md#ability-technological-singularity). Destroyer II’s Anti-Fighter Barrage can destroy an opponent’s unit during combat, creating a stated opportunity for the combat technology gain. Sources: [SCPT 323, 1590.86–1648.38s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/323-super-nekro-virus-guide/)
- [Imperial](../components.md#strategy-card-pok8imperial) **scores** [The Nekro Virus](nekro.md). The guide recommends an Imperial pick when it can secure a bonus point such as Mecatol Rex, unless doing so diverts too much plastic or creates unacceptable risk. Sources: [SCPT 323, 6331.44–6367.08s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/323-super-nekro-virus-guide/)

## Strategy claims

<a id="claim-c01"></a>

- **Draft:** Treat the opening as a recovery phase: the starting Dreadnought gives fleet presence, but only two infantry and one Carrier leave limited capacity and weak early ground reach; prioritize plastic and expansion before chasing a technology engine.
  Conditions: Especially relevant in round one and when the slice does not compensate with extra infantry, capacity, or a suitable objective. Compatibility: Episode 323, published 2023-11-01; guide says Nekro had no direct post-POK change at recording, but current compatibility is unreviewed. Uncertainty: The speakers agree the infantry opening is weak; their tournament win-rate explanations are explicitly speculative.
  Sources: [SCPT 323 1161–1200s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/323-super-nekro-virus-guide/) · [SCPT 323 6166–6178s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/323-super-nekro-virus-guide/)
  Components: [The Nekro Virus](nekro.md), [The Alastor](../components.md#unit-nekro-flagship)
<a id="claim-c02"></a>

- **Draft:** In round one, prefer another player taking Warfare; if no one will and the secondary is needed to repair the opening, take Warfare yourself, even when Trade is also attractive. Opponents can pressure Nekro by making it spend its own pick on Warfare.
  Conditions: Opening pick depends on other factions’ Warfare needs, pick order, and whether Warfare primary/secondary unlocks the required expansion. Compatibility: Episode 323 advice; no current rules or meta verification. Uncertainty: The presenters strongly prioritize Warfare over Trade for Nekro’s opening, while acknowledging this is situational and may not generalize to every Warfare-reliant faction.
  Sources: [SCPT 323 3747–3797s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/323-super-nekro-virus-guide/) · [SCPT 323 4976–5017s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/323-super-nekro-virus-guide/)
  Components: [Warfare](../components.md#strategy-card-pok6warfare), [Trade](../components.md#strategy-card-pok5trade), [The Nekro Virus](nekro.md)
<a id="claim-c03"></a>

- **Draft:** Do not spend the round-one economy primarily on Leadership tokens or Technology-secondary research when the opening still needs ships and infantry. Nekro cannot research; a Technology primary/secondary converts the research step into three command tokens, so buying plastic can address the more immediate bottleneck.
  Conditions: Applies when early expansion or an objective is constrained by plastic; taking Leadership or following a strategy secondary can still be right when token demand or another objective requires it. Compatibility: Episode 323 guide; distinction reflects the speakers’ interpretation and is not an independent rules ruling. Uncertainty: The submitted pre-errata recommendation is endorsed by the host, but its wording ‘unless you spend 3 tokens’ is unclear in ASR; the narrower plastic-first advice is clear.
  Sources: [SCPT 323 4539–4576s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/323-super-nekro-virus-guide/) · [SCPT 323 1657–1752s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/323-super-nekro-virus-guide/)
  Components: [Leadership](../components.md#strategy-card-pok1leadership), [Technology](../components.md#strategy-card-pok7technology), [The Nekro Virus](nekro.md)
<a id="claim-c04"></a>

- **Draft:** Trade is an excellent opening when it can fund plastic and payments that keep a target ship from retreating, but it is secondary to securing needed Warfare in the speakers’ recommended priority. Evaluate both cards against the opening bottleneck instead of treating Trade as automatic.
  Conditions: Most useful when Trade is available without leaving Nekro unable to expand; if no one else takes essential Warfare, Warfare takes precedence in this guide. Compatibility: Episode 323 strategy-card discussion; compatibility unreviewed. Uncertainty: This is a ranking in the episode rather than a universal pick order.
  Sources: [SCPT 323 4957–5000s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/323-super-nekro-virus-guide/)
  Components: [Trade](../components.md#strategy-card-pok5trade), [Warfare](../components.md#strategy-card-pok6warfare)
<a id="claim-c05"></a>

- **Draft:** Track opponents’ technology acquisitions and plan small, controlled combats around them. The guide recommends a ‘tortoise’ approach: negotiate a modest target ship, pay its owner not to retreat, then destroy it to gain the technology while avoiding an unnecessarily costly early invasion.
  Conditions: Requires an opponent with a technology worth acquiring, a combat that can destroy one of their units, and a deal that is cheaper than forcing the fight; adapt to each opponent and board state. Compatibility: Episode 323 cites an older base-game essay; speakers say its slow-roll philosophy remains useful, while its component-specific advice may be outdated. Uncertainty: The referenced essay is not among assigned documents; claim is limited to the episode’s description of it and the hosts’ endorsement.
  Sources: [SCPT 323 3971–4038s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/323-super-nekro-virus-guide/)
  Components: [Technological Singularity](../components.md#ability-technological-singularity), [The Nekro Virus](nekro.md)
<a id="claim-c06"></a>

- **Draft:** Make the no-retreat arrangement reciprocal: explain which ship Nekro wants to destroy, agree where the combat occurs, and compensate the opponent for losing the ship. The hosts reject the idea that opponents should donate technology access for free.
  Conditions: For negotiated technology gains early, when the opponent can allow a small loss without undermining their own position. Compatibility: Episode 323 podcast advice; no rules or etiquette standard is asserted. Uncertainty: Deal terms and payment amount are left to negotiation.
  Sources: [SCPT 323 6000–6048s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/323-super-nekro-virus-guide/)
  Components: [Technological Singularity](../components.md#ability-technological-singularity)
<a id="claim-c07"></a>

- **Draft:** Use the timing of Technological Singularity to gain technologies from units destroyed during combat, including Anti-Fighter Barrage and separate space and ground combats in the same activation. Look for multi-combat activations when several opponents’ units can be destroyed, rather than expecting non-combat destruction to qualify.
  Conditions: The episode describes the ability as once per combat and only when an opponent’s unit is destroyed in combat; each separate combat may offer another opportunity. Compatibility: Episode 323 rules discussion; independent current-rules verification remains outstanding. Uncertainty: The hosts suggest as many as four gains in one activation as an illustrative possibility, not a routine outcome.
  Sources: [SCPT 323 1464–1509s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/323-super-nekro-virus-guide/) · [SCPT 323 1510–1573s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/323-super-nekro-virus-guide/)
  Components: [Technological Singularity](../components.md#ability-technological-singularity)
<a id="claim-c08"></a>

- **Draft:** Destroyer II is an attractive combat target because improved Anti-Fighter Barrage can destroy enemy units before later combat rounds and still trigger the technology ability; ordinary Destroyer II is useful even if Argent’s Strike Wing Alpha II is unavailable.
  Conditions: Best when opponents field fighters and Nekro can afford the destroyers; the guide calls Argent’s upgrade an ideal but exceptional version. Compatibility: Episode 323; the discussion’s interaction and value are not independently rules-checked. Uncertainty: A community submission proposes bargaining for Argent’s upgrade; the hosts endorse destroyers generally and describe the special upgrade as best case.
  Sources: [SCPT 323 1591–1648s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/323-super-nekro-virus-guide/)
  Components: [Destroyer II](../components.md#technology-dd2), [Destroyer II](../components.md#unit-destroyer2), [Strike Wing Alpha II](../components.md#unit-argent-destroyer2), [Technological Singularity](../components.md#ability-technological-singularity)
<a id="claim-c09"></a>

- **Draft:** Distinguish gaining a technology from researching one: the guide says Nekro’s copied technologies do not require prerequisites, while effects that would research instead yield three command tokens. It contrasts this with effects that explicitly gain a technology, which can still grant one.
  Conditions: Use the distinction when resolving strategy-card secondaries, action cards, or other effects; the episode names Maw of Worlds as an example of gaining rather than researching. Compatibility: Episode 323 explanation, offered as rules interpretation; not a current-rules ruling. Uncertainty: The discussion’s exact edge cases may depend on card wording and edition; check current component text before applying.
  Sources: [SCPT 323 1657–1752s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/323-super-nekro-virus-guide/)
  Components: [The Nekro Virus](nekro.md), [Technology](../components.md#strategy-card-pok7technology)
<a id="claim-c10"></a>

- **Draft:** Treat Valefar Assimilator X and Y as two limited faction-text slots: on a qualifying technology gain, Nekro may put a token on an opponent’s faction technology and use its text. Replacing a copied unit-upgrade text can reveal the underlying upgrade again, so changing a token does not necessarily erase Nekro’s original upgrade.
